supports.excerpt:
## 
 In this article

The routing capabilities in a virtual hub are provided by a router that manages all routing between gateways using Border Gateway Protocol (BGP). A virtual hub can contain multiple gateways such as a Site-to-site VPN gateway, ExpressRoute gateway, Point-to-site gateway, Azure Firewall. This router also provides transit connectivity between virtual networks that connect to a virtual hub and can support up to an aggregate throughput of 50 Gbps. These routing capabilities apply to Standard Virtual WAN customers.

To configure routing, see How to configure virtual hub routing.

metadata.prompt: Use this reference to understand core virtual hub routing concepts. A virtual hub router manages all routing between gateways using BGP and can contain multiple gateway types (Site-to-site VPN, ExpressRoute, Point-to-site, Azure Firewall). The router provides transit connectivity between virtual networks and supports up to 50 Gbps aggregate throughput. Key concepts include: route tables (organize and filter routes), routing intents and policies (define traffic forwarding rules), connections (link gateways and virtual networks), association (connect routes to connections), propagation (distribute routes across the hub), and labels (tag routes for policy application). Static routes can be configured in virtual network connections for custom routing behavior.
